newsitem.title: JAPAN: Lawyers hope witnesses will ease Hamanaka sentence.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers hope witnesses will ease Hamanaka sentence.

text.p: A lawyer for Yasuo Hamanaka, the once influential copper trader who pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery, said on Tuesday the defense hoped to summon six current and former Sumitomo managers to give evidence in mitigation at his trial.

Toru Yoshiki, one of Hamanaka's team of lawyers, told Reuters he hoped the witnesses' testimony would lead judges to give Hamanaka a lighter sentence. Hamanaka faces a maximum 15 years in prison under the fraud and forgery charges.

One of the managers, Saburo Shimizu, was Hamanaka's boss at Sumitomo Corp in the late 1980s when, prosecutors said, he first began racking up losses from unauthorised trading that eventually snowballed to $2.6 billion.
The lawyers entered a motion to summon the six on Monday, the opening day of Hamanaka's trial.
Only one of the witnesses, Yoshio Takeuchi of the trade house's credit control department, has been approved. He is scheduled to appear at the next hearing on March 10.
Yoshiki said Takeuchi was approved immediately because he was also the lone witness called by prosecutors.
He said the defense wanted to call Takeuchi in order to question the adequacy of checks and controls at Sumitomo headquarters.
He also said he hoped that Shimizu, who until he quit around August 1987 was leader of Sumitomo's copper team and Hamanaka's boss, would shed light on the origin of Hamanaka's unauthorised deals.

Prosecutors said in their opening statement on Monday that Shimizu and Hamanaka began unauthorised, speculative trading in London Metal Exchange futures in 1985, in an effort to sustain the copper team's profitability after it had recorded its first full-year profit in 10 years.

But they incurred losses that they eventually hid through off-the-book deals, and by the time Shimizu quit the company in 1987 and Hamanaka took over as team leader, their losses had climbed to 6.5 billion yen.
Yoshiki said the defense also moved to call three officials from a Sumitomo Hong Kong subsidiary, although it was unclear at this point whether all three would be summoned.
